I created `docs/policies/async-runtime.md`. It says the project's current recorded decision is tokio, chosen because its ecosystem is bigger. I didn't commit it.

The decision comes from the claude-mem prompt history, not from the repo, which has no mention of an async runtime. The history has an earlier prompt, "async-std runtime", followed at 3:29 PM by "tokio, ecosystem is bigger". I treated the later one as current and left async-std out of the file, as you asked.

The memory returned only your prompts, with no observations or session summaries. It gave me short titles and no full text. So the file rests on those two prompts, and I couldn't confirm whether the tokio prompt was meant as a firm decision. This checkout is also a Go project (Gin), so tokio has no obvious place in the code itself.
